peircean_analysis.firstness: Two Sony Ericsson T630 memory dumps: images.bin (active, 12MB) and images-deleted.bin (forensic recovery, 12MB). First 8MB identical (firmware). At byte 8388610: images.bin has header 1f260300 + near-zero user partition (wiped); images-deleted.bin has header 1f250400 + 3,863,179 non-null bytes of RGB565 photo data (recovered photographs). Java MIDlet game (Q*bert) also present in recovered partition.
peircean_analysis.secondness: The user data partition was zeroed between the active state and the forensic recovery capture. The forensic tool recovered 3.86MB of deleted images. The cleaning appears total — the entire user partition was wiped, not selective files. However: on Sony Ericsson T630, 'delete all pictures' produces byte-for-byte identical zeroing pattern to a deliberate anti-forensic wipe. Both operations clear the user partition. No selective targeting of specific content visible.
peircean_analysis.thirdness: Could be: (A) user deleted photos to free storage space — completely routine on a 12MB total flash device, or (B) deliberate anti-forensic wipe of potentially sensitive images. No evidence differentiates (A) from (B) — no anti-forensic tool artifacts, no targeted selective deletion, no context about investigation trigger.

hypotheses.H1_anti_forensic_wipe: User deliberately zeroed image partition to prevent forensic recovery of sensitive photographs.
hypotheses.H2_routine_deletion: User deleted photos to free storage space on a capacity-constrained device. Normal behavior, byte-identical to anti-forensic wipe.

refutation_protocol.benign_hypothesis: Routine 'delete all pictures' on a 12MB Sony Ericsson T630 phone is the dominant explanation. No forensic awareness indicators present. The case devil_advocate is explicit: 'Most users delete photos to free space, not to hide evidence.'
refutation_protocol.test_result: H2 SURVIVES fully. Cannot be distinguished from H1 on available evidence. SUSPICION is the defensible cap.
refutation_protocol.refutation_outcome: H1 neither proven nor refuted. SUSPICION maintained.

devil_advocate: Normal 'delete all pictures' on this device produces the exact same binary signature as a targeted anti-forensic wipe. The pedagogical context (challenge designed to teach photo recovery) suggests the intended lesson is about recovery capability, not deliberate anti-forensics. No other indicators of forensic awareness.
evidence_anchors: SET630-ART-002: byte 8388610 divergence — user partition wiped in images.bin, recovered in images-deleted.bin
SET630-ART-003: 3,863,179 bytes of RGB565 image data recovered from deleted partition
carnegie_pattern: Possible: data hiding via targeted memory zeroing — but routine deletion is indistinguishable
known_limitations: No context about why photos were deleted. No forensic awareness indicators. Challenge dataset — pedagogical context suggests photo recovery demonstration, not criminal investigation.
